Analysis Loolkit for Large Studies of Bisulfite-sequencing : ATLAS²


ATLAS² is a Nextflow-based pipeline for reproducible, scalable, and comprehensive analysis of bisulfite sequencing data. Designed for both newly generated and publicly available datasets, it performs extensive quality control, preprocessing, alignment, methylation calling, and exploratory analyses. With detailed reports and standardized outputs, ATLAS² delivers analysis-ready results that can be directly used for visualization, statistical modeling, and downstream epigenomic studies, from small experiments to large scale studies

title: How to launch the pipeline
text:
First, we will need to install conda (if not available) with the following command in a linux terminal
sudo apt install conda
Then using conda, we will create a new conda environment with Nextflow v25.10.4 (this version is the last one using the old parser in which the ATLAS² was coded)
cd path/to/where/you/want/the/environment/to/be ## optional but it's better to know where your environment will be created
conda create -p ./env -c conda-forge -c bioconda --override-channels nextflow=25.10.4

title: How to launch the pipeline
text:
Launch the pipeline

Now with the conda environment created, we will need to activate this environment
conda activate ./env/ #assuming you are in the correct directory, i.e the "path/to/where/you/want/the/environment/to/be" from before
After activating the conda environment, we can check if the right version of Nextflow is installed
nextflow -version
The following output should be printed
N E X T F L O W
      version 25.10.4 build 11173
      created XX-XX-XXXX XX:XX UTC (XX:XX CEST)
      cite doi:10.1038/nbt.3820
      http://nextflow.io
Now, you can theoretically launch any Nextflow pipeline using this conda environment, for example ATLAS², we can launch the pipeline with the following command
nextflow run main.nf 
But as you can see if you run the command above, we actually need to have the pipeline stored locally to be able to use main.nf, which contains the pipeline’s code.
 Future update might allow to skip this step entirely by directly launching the pipeline from a repository

title: How to launch the pipeline
text:
Retrieve the pipeline online

The pipeline can be found in this following public Github repository. You can clone this repository to have everything locally
## change your directory to where you want the pipeline to be stored
git clone https://github.com/ottarein/atlas-bis.git
Now, place yourself inside the pipeline directory you just cloned. From the root of that directory, running ls should show the following
modules nextflow.config params.yml ref_genome samplesheet.csv subworkflow
test-files, modules, ref_genome, subworkflow are folders while nextflow.config, params.yml, samplesheet.csv should be files.

title: Welcome to ATLAS²
text:
ATLAS² (pronounced atlas-bis) is a powerful and reproducible Nextflow-based pipeline designed for comprehensive analysis of bisulfite sequencing data. Built to support both newly generated datasets and publicly available sequencing data, ATLAS² streamlines the entire processing workflow from raw reads to analysis-ready results.
Whether analyzing a single experiment or large-scale cohort studies involving hundreds of samples, ATLAS² provides a scalable and robust framework that ensures consistency, reproducibility, and ease of deployment across computing environments.
The pipeline performs extensive quality assessment at every stage of the analysis, generating detailed reports that allow users to evaluate sequencing quality, alignment performance, bisulfite conversion efficiency, coverage metrics, and methylation calling accuracy. Beyond quality control, ATLAS² includes a suite of preliminary analyses that help users rapidly explore their datasets and identify potential technical or biological patterns before conducting in-depth investigations.
All outputs are organized into standardized, analysis-ready formats, enabling seamless integration with downstream visualization tools, statistical frameworks, and custom bioinformatics workflows. By combining automation, comprehensive reporting, and scalability, ATLAS² empowers researchers to efficiently process and explore bisulfite sequencing datasets while maintaining full reproducibility and transparency.
From raw sequencing data to publication-ready analyses, ATLAS² provides a complete foundation for large-scale epigenomic studies.
